s1.syndrome_frame: subacute febrile illness with back pain and multiple organ involvement
salient_findings: fever and back pain lasting 3 weeks
key_facts: 76-year-old Japanese man
presented with fever and back pain
endoscopic treatment for common bile duct stones 3 weeks prior
medical history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension
taking cilnidipine and metformin hydrochloride
social history of smoking and ethanol consumption
temperature 37.8°C
elevated CRP (22.1 mg/dL) and WBC (11,910/μL)
low platelet count (10.3 × 10^4/μL)
elevated ALP (275 U/L) and low albumin (1.7 g/dL)
abnormal fasting blood glucose (280 mg/dL) and HbA1c (9.3%)
multiple hypodense lesions in right liver lobe on abdominal CT
echogenicity-mixed hypoechoic lesion without blood flow on abdominal ultrasonography
gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining
positive cultures (blood, urine, and abscess fluid) for identified organism

shortlist.label: Infective Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: fever, back pain, elevated CRP and WBC, and multiple organ involvement

shortlist.label: Bacterial Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining and positive cultures

shortlist.label: Pott's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: back pain and multiple hypodense lesions in right liver lobe on abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Nocardiosis
shortlist.why_kept: subacute febrile illness with back pain and multiple organ involvement, and gram-negative bacilli on Gram staining

shortlist.label: Brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: fever, back pain, and elevated CRP and WBC, with a history of possible exposure to infectious agents

raw.rationale: The patient presented with fever and back pain, and imaging studies showed enlarged high-signal areas in the L4/5 intervertebral disc, which is consistent with spinal infection. The presence of low-density area of left-sided iliopsoas muscle swelling and multiple cavitated nodules in lungs also supports the diagnosis of Pott's Disease, which is a form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis that can affect the spine and other organs.

rejected.label: Infective Endocarditis
rejected.why: No heart murmur, Osler's nodes, or Janeway lesions were present, which are common findings in infective endocarditis.

rejected.label: Bacterial Endocarditis
rejected.why: Similar to infective endocarditis, the absence of cardiac findings makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Nocardiosis
rejected.why: While Nocardiosis can cause abscesses and systemic infection, the patient's presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with Pott's Disease.

rejected.label: Brucellosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not strongly suggest Brucellosis, and the imaging findings are more consistent with Pott's Disease.
